name: black pudding

special_abilities.name: amorphous
special_abilities.desc: The pudding can move through a space as narrow as 1 inch wide without squeezing.

special_abilities.name: corrosive form
special_abilities.desc: A creature that touches the pudding or hits it with a melee attack while within 5 feet of it takes 4 (1d8) acid damage. Any nonmagical weapon made of metal or wood that hits the pudding corrodes. After dealing damage, the weapon takes a permanent and cumulative -1 penalty to damage rolls. If its penalty drops to -5, the weapon is destroyed. Nonmagical ammunition made of metal or wood that hits the pudding is destroyed after dealing damage. The pudding can eat through 2-inch-thick, nonmagical wood or metal in 1 round.

special_abilities.name: spider climb
special_abilities.desc: The pudding can climb difficult surfaces, including upside down on ceilings, without needing to make an ability check.

actions.name: pseudopod
actions.desc: Melee Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 6 (1d6 + 3) bludgeoning damage plus 18 (4d8) acid damage. In addition, nonmagical armor worn by the target is partly dissolved and takes a permanent and cumulative -1 penalty to the AC it offers. The armor is destroyed if the penalty reduces its AC to 10.

reactions.name: split
reactions.desc: When a pudding that is Medium or larger is subjected to lightning or slashing damage, it splits into two new puddings if it has at least 10 hit points. Each new pudding has hit points equal to half the original pudding's, rounded down. New puddings are one size smaller than the original pudding.

lore:
The Black Pudding, or *Amorphus tenebris*, is a silent horror of the deep places. It dwells in the lightless veins of the world—damp caverns, forgotten vaults, and the stagnant arteries of ancient sewers. It is not a creature of bone and sinew, but a singular, obsidian mass of corrosive hunger.

Its predation is a slow, agonizing dissolution. Lacking eyes, it senses the faint tremors of heat and movement. When it strikes, it flows like spilled ink, its acidic touch liquefying plate armor and parching flesh in heartbeats. To strike it with a blade is folly; one merely invites the horror to divide, birthing two hungers from one.

In the fireside tales of the Deep-Delvers, the Pudding is whispered to be the "Bile of the Earth," a manifestation of the world's desire to reclaim what was stolen from its depths. To the superstitious, it is a living curse—a reminder that in the dark, even the shadows can hunger. Tread softly, traveler, for where the stone weeps black, death follows in a silent crawl.
